articles.title: 重点整治滥用 AI 技术生成健康科普谣言等，中央网信办部署开展专项行动
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，为进一步加强科普健康领域网络谣言突出问题整治，营造风清气正网络空间，近日，中央网信办印发通知，在全国范围内部署开展为期 2 个月的“清朗 · 整治科普健康类网络谣言”专项行动。中央网信办有关负责同志表示，本次专项行动重点整治以下 4 方面突出问题：（一）编造民生健康网络谣言，借机误导网民。一是以关注公众健康等为名义，将普通食品、保健品包装成“神药”，推广所谓“包治百病”偏方，发布伪科普信息，借审美焦虑制造“黄连素是减肥神药”等运动、减重类谣言。二是刻意夸大食品、药品、生活用品副作用，配以夸张骇人标题，编造所谓“长期服用降压药会使血管变脆”“献血会伤害身体”“味精加热有毒”“蜂蜜结晶不能吃”等缺乏科学依据、断章取义的谣言信息，制造焦虑恐慌情绪。三是以“科学辟谣”“现代医学真相”等名义，发表“某类食物全是智商税”“某项常规检查完全没必要”“肯定致癌”等极端化、绝对化论断，使用“揭露被掩盖的真相”“医生不会告诉你的秘方”等语言否定权威机构，甚至鼓动自我诊断、拒绝就医，误导公众。四是打着“古法养生”“古法育儿”“国粹养生”等旗号，鼓吹“胎里吃素”“中国人不需要蛋白质”，对传统文化进行片面解读甚至恶意歪曲，通过“能量玄学”“命理疗疾”等方式传播封建迷信思想。（二）冒用专业身份等，传播伪科学观点。一是冒充医疗卫生健康等领域专业人士或正规机构人员，离职人员沿用原单位和职务信息认证，违规开展网络健康科普。二是打造所谓“国家一级保健师”“国家一级营养师”等，或者身着专业服装在医院、诊室等场景进行摆拍，散播没有科学依据的“食疗”“偏方”。三是包装虚假专家、“先知”等，编造所谓“量子赋能”“宇宙能量”等伪科学概念，兜售假冒伪劣产品。四是打着“网红大师”“得道高人”等名义，宣称掌握“能量玄学密码”可治病消灾，利用部分群体焦虑心理非法牟利。（三）滥用人工智能技术，生成健康科普谣言。一是利用 AI 技术批量生成同质化涉健康科普类文案、图片、音视频，制造虚假舆论热点，推销相关产品。二是利用 AI 换脸、换声技术盗用知名专家形象、声音，进行虚假科普、带货。三是诱导 AI 大模型生成并传播虚假“死亡率”“存活率”、不实科学数据等谣言，借机售卖保健品。四是利用 AI 生成伪造权威通报、官方健康提示、夸大疗效等图片、视频信息，借机误导网民。（四）虚构康复案例夸大疗效，通过私域等环节诱骗消费。一是以“亲身经历”“患者康复故事”“祖传秘方”“专家私授”等为幌子，编造虚假故事、康复案例，声称“100% 有效”“永不复发”，并提供所谓前后对比图、聊天截图夸大功效，引至私信、群聊等私域环节进行诈骗。二是过度渲染食品、保健养生品等的营养成分，夸大医疗设备的功能作用，进行营销带货。三是以“专家私域讲课”“会员专享”等为包装，在社群等私域场景内开展虚假宣传，通过送礼品领红包、情感诱导等方式欺骗老年消费者。IT之家获悉，网信部门将采取以下治理措施：一是加大违规账号和机构查处力度。从严处置生成传播健康科普网络谣言、扰乱网络生态秩序的违法违规账号。强化医疗科普等账号身份资质核验认证，要求清晰展示账号资质信息，不得以账号简介处标注“某医院医师”“某领域专家”等形式进行模糊暗示，严格标注医疗科普信息来源。二是加强重点环节管理。严禁在榜单、推荐等位置推送科普健康类谣言信息。建立科普谣言信息关键词库和典型案例库，扩大权威科普内容池，及时标记辟谣标签，并通过弹窗、私信提醒等方式强化辟谣信息触达。三是提升平台 AI 防治能力。督促平台提升对 AI 生成合成涉科普健康谣言信息的发现、识别和处置能力，强化 AI 换脸、换声、虚拟人形象检测和深度合成鉴伪，对假冒专业领域人员内容实现自动化识别。中央网信办有关负责同志强调，各地网信部门要充分认识到开展专项行动的重要意义，切实履行属地管理责任，强化部门协同联动，形成整治工作合力，督导网站平台对照整治重点，聚焦重点环节、版块深入自查自纠，全面排查问题漏洞，定期对外发布典型案例，强化警示震慑效应，帮助广大网民更好辨别科普健康领域网络谣言，不造谣、不信谣、不传谣，确保专项行动取得实效。

articles.title: 异能者推出 Windows & Android 双系统二合一设备，基于 Ultra 5 115U
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，异能者 (ERAZER) 现已推出二合一设备 U126。其本体采用平板电脑形态，随附磁吸背光键盘，支持 Windows 11 / Android 16 双操作系统。异能者 U126 拥有全金属机身，薄至 8.5mm，质量 760g。其基于英特尔酷睿 Ultra 5 处理器 115U，配备 LPDDR5 内存、SSD 存储，拥有一块 12.6" 2560×1600 60Hz 450nits OLED 屏幕，集成 2 个 1W 扬声器、5MP 后摄，支持 Wi-Fi & 蓝牙 5.0，内置 40.425Whr 电池。异能者 U126 二合一 8GB + 512GB 配置到手价 5,499 元、12GB + 512GB 配置到手价 5,999 元。京东异能者 U126 二合一 5499 元起直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 群联 2026 财年前三季度报归母净利润 719.38 亿新台币
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，群联今日发布 2026 财年（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 12 月）前三季度报（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 9 月）报告： 营业总收入：1949.32 亿新台币（IT之家注：现汇率约合 394.93 亿元人民币） 毛利润：1208.39 亿新台币（现汇率约合 244.82 亿元人民币） 毛利率：62.01% 归母净利润：719.38 亿新台币（现汇率约合 145.75 亿元人民币） 基本每股收益：325.49 新台币（现汇率约合 65.94 元人民币） 资产负债率：49.62% AI 解读 群联电子2026年前三季度累计营收达 1949.32 亿新台币（现汇率约合 394.93 亿元人民币）、归母净利润 719.38 亿新台币（现汇率约合 145.75 亿元人民币）、基本每股盈余 325.49 新台币（现汇率约合 65.94 元人民币），大幅领先市场机构此前对前三季度盈利的普遍预期，全年获利上看新台币 400 元以上的机构预期区间。公司主营业务与本期财报亮点群联电子为全球 NAND Flash 控制芯片与存储模组龙头，主要产品涵盖 SSD 控制芯片、eSSD 企业级存储、AI 生态模组（含 aiDAPTIV、AI PC、AI 服务器、开机盘等），深度受益于 AI 推理需求爆发与 NAND Flash 供需结构性缺货。2026 年前三季度累计营收 1949.32 亿新台币（现汇率约合 394.93 亿元人民币），创历年同期新高；AI 生态模组营收占比已超过整体营收的 50%，成为核心成长动能。前三季度归母净利润 719.38 亿新台币（现汇率约合 145.75 亿元人民币），对应基本每股盈余 325.49 新台币（现汇率约合 65.94 元人民币），盈利规模显著放大。累计营业毛利 1208.39 亿新台币（现汇率约合 244.82 亿元人民币），毛利率约 62.01%，处于历史高位区间，反映 NAND 涨价红利与高毛利 AI 产品占比提升。期末总资产 2372.38 亿新台币（现汇率约合 480.64 亿元人民币）、总负债 1177.18 亿新台币（现汇率约合 238.5 亿元人民币），资产负债率约 49.62%，财务结构稳健。未来展望与投资价值公司当前仅能满足约 30%–35% 的客户需求，预期 NAND 缺货情况下半年较上半年更严峻，2027 年供需仍偏紧；机构预估 2026 年全年税后 EPS 上看新台币 401.94 元，2027 年营收有望进一步成长。当前股价对应估值在高景气周期下仍具成长空间，分析师共识评级为买进，12 个月目标价显著高于现价。 相关阅读： 《华虹宏力 2026 财年第三财季归母净利润 1.23 亿美元，同比增长 147.1%》 《Arm 2027 财年第二财季归母净利润 1.3 亿美元，同比下降 45%》 《高通 2026 财年归母净利润 136.28 亿美元同比增长 146%，与苹果、华为续签长期技术授权许可协议》 《格罗方德 2026 财年第三财季归母亏损 2.7 亿美元，同比下降 208%》 《南亚科技 2026 财年前三季度报归母净利润 1638.79 亿新台币》 《群联 2026 财年第一财季净利润 151.74 亿元新台币》 风险提示：本文内容由 AI 自动分析生成，仅供参考，不代表IT之家观点。如有出入请以证监会指定上市公司信息披露平台为准。本文内容不构成投资建议，如有投资者据此操作，风险自担，IT之家对此不承担任何责任。

articles.title: 华为 Mate 90 系列手机获 HarmonyOS 7.0.0.111SP15 升级，优化搭配睿影 Z10 模块相机的拍摄效果
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，华为今日面向 Mate 90 系列手机推送了鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 7.0.0.111 SP15 版本升级，系统包大小约 727.57MB。▲ IT之家实拍：华为 Mate 90 Pro Max 典藏版据介绍，本次更新优化了在搭配华为睿影 Z10 模块相机时的拍摄效果，并同时优化了整机系统稳定性。据IT之家了解，华为睿影 Z10 模块相机代号“金刚”，集成红枫等多种传感器，支持与手机 SoC 协同，通过软硬芯 AI 协同 + 智能融合对焦，实现对焦快、准、稳；拥有独立光学防抖模块，与麒麟芯片协同，可实现旗舰级防抖体验。

articles.title: 高通 CEO 安蒙：6G 从设计之初就具备 AI 原生特性，目标 2029 年商用
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，在本周的 2026 移动网络大会上，高通公司总裁兼 CEO 安蒙表示，6G 从设计之初就将具备 AI 原生特性，让 AI 融入网络本身。安蒙称，借助网络连接，上下文信息可以持续在终端、边缘和云端之间交换。AI 将直接融入无线通信系统，使系统在估计信道状况的基础上，还能预测其变化，即使信号较弱，也能保持性能。此外，计算将遍布整个网络，从基站到网络边缘，再到数据中心。这样，AI 计算和推理任务可以分布在网络的不同节点上执行。今年 9 月，高通与中国移动在全球首次完成了 U6G 频段基站原型和 6G 终端原型互通测试，测试基于最新的 3GPP 定义开展。安蒙表示，这是 6G 从技术研究迈向系统验证的重要一步。高通与中国移动也在共同推进 AI 原生网络技术和新的无线通信能力的发展，整个行业正朝着 2029 年启动 6G 商用的目标迈进。IT之家 11 月 5 日在第九届中国国际进口博览会（进博会）现场看到，高通展示了全球首个 6G 终端原型机。这是高通连续第九年参加进博会，今年展台的重头戏，就是全球首个符合 3GPP 最新定义的 6G 终端原型机首次走出实验室，公开实物亮相。进博局也给原型机贴上了“硬科技展品”和“全球首展”标签。该原型机已用于与中国移动、中兴通讯等中国产业伙伴的联合 6G 技术测试和互操作验证。在今年 8 月的高通全球 6G 分析师与媒体日上，高通执行副总裁、边缘解决方案与数据中心业务总经理马德嘉（Durga Malladi）接受了包括IT之家在内的媒体专访，详细阐述了高通的 6G 战略与数据中心布局。随着全球通信技术向 6G 时代加速迭代，通信、人工智能与算力产业的边界正快速消融，行业迎来技术范式与商业模式的双重变革。相较于 5G 时代聚焦移动宽带普及的发展路径，预定 2029 年商用落地的 6G，以 AI 原生、通感一体、全域算力协同为核心特质，重构终端形态、网络架构与产业生态，成为全球科技巨头角逐的核心赛道。在终端形态上，马德嘉认为 6G 时代将催生一批全新的设备类别，他称之为“智能体 AI 设备”，并指出这一趋势在中国已经出现。

articles.title: 谷歌为 Googlebook 带来 11 月更新：端侧 AI 性能占用降低，最多释放 6GB 内存
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，据科技媒体 Android Authority 今天报道，谷歌现已为 Googlebook 笔记本带来 11 月更新，包含 30 项修复和改进，并更新 2026 年 11 月安全补丁。谷歌表示，本次更新有效降低了端侧 AI 的内存占用，释放 3GB-6GB 内存。上述改进可让笔记本获得更流畅的使用体验，打开大量标签页、处理高负载任务时，设备性能将得到提升，标签页重新加载和崩溃的情况有所减少。IT之家注意到，本次更新还修复了二合一设备的键盘 / 触控板输入无响应问题，以及使用 Zoom 多种特效时发生崩溃、使用显示器播放受 DRM 保护的视频时出现黑屏、外接 USB 麦克风无法使用等问题。其他修复还包括减少蓝牙耳机音频延迟、确保蓝牙 LE 鼠标在设备重启后能够可靠地重新连接、修复多项 Linux 终端问题，以及提升 60fps HDR 视频播放的稳定性。

articles.title: 全华班团队：比亚迪仰望 U9X“地表最快量产车”研发工程师揭秘，平均年龄不足 30 岁
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，比亚迪仰望汽车官方今日宣布，仰望 U9X 阿布扎比公共道路极速挑战，以 503.17km/h 的成绩再创全球极速新纪录。IT之家从比亚迪官方获悉，该成绩于 11 月 1 日在阿联酋阿布扎比 E11 高速公路的封闭测试路段取得，并由车手马克 · 巴森（Marc Basseng）担纲驾驶。另外，本次项目的车辆研发工程师，均来自仰望内部研发团队，平均年龄不足 30 岁。这支“全华班”团队从 2024 年开始，伴随仰望 U9 及 U9 Xtreme 持续开展测试，逐步挑战世界纪录。比亚迪官方表示，仰望 U9X 各系统在高负荷下的协同能力至关重要。该车采用仰望 U9 同根同源的易四方与云辇-X 创新技术架构，搭载四个 30000rpm 高性能电机，整车拥有超 3000Ps 综合马力，推重比高达 1217Ps/t。另外，仰望 U9X 还搭载了全域 1200V 超高压平台、30C 赛道级刀片电池与热管理系统的协同、3D 打印一体化车身与超级碳舱组成的超级车身架构、超 500km/h 时速定制轮胎。

articles.title: 全球首台 4000 米级浮空风电系统在湖南岳阳完成城市首飞
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，据央视新闻报道，全球首台 4000 米级浮空风力发电系统今日（11 月 6 日）在湖南岳阳成功试飞，这是 4000 米级浮空风电系统首次在城市场景完成放飞试验。此次完成放飞验证的 S4000 浮空风力发电系统，长度达到 67 米，宽 40 米、高 23 米，升空海拔可达 4000 米，输出电压覆盖 10 千伏至 35 千伏，设计使用寿命 20 年。该系统通过充氦浮空平台将轻量化发电模块送至数千米高空，利用高空稳定的风资源持续发电，发出的电再经系留缆绳送回地面。浮空风力发电系统首席架构设计师顿天瑞介绍，今天更多要测试的是其接网的性能，开着发电机的情况下，是否会对电力和姿态稳定性造成干扰。城市试飞考验的是“能不能安全、可靠地在市民、在人群周边进行飞行”。城市才是耗电的核心区域，最终还是要让这些供电系统，向着人口更密集的区域迈进。高空风能作为尚未规模开发的新能源“无人区”，具有风速高、风向稳定、风能密度大等优势，蕴藏着巨大潜力。IT之家了解到，目前高空风能发电主要有陆基和空基两种技术路线：陆基把重型发电机留在地面，靠翼伞、浮空器等空中组件牵引缆绳做功；空基则把发电机组随浮空器送上天空，在高空就地发电。S4000 浮空风力发电系统今年 8 月，在西北某试验基地完成 4000 米全流程验证，验证了高原、强紫外线、大温差条件下的极限适应性。中国科学院空天信息创新研究院研究员蔡榕介绍，本次城市场景试飞验证了整套浮空系统的可靠性，也验证了在城市周边真实工况下完成工程交付的可能性和完整性，以及现场快速部署的能力，打通了研发、试验、运行的关键链路，为适航取证、场景示范铺路，有力推动高空风力发电装备从技术验证走向产业化落地。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，北京市市场监督管理局公示信息显示，中国石油集团昆仑制造有限公司（“昆仑制造”）及其一致行动人昆仑资本，拟与宇树科技股份有限公司（“宇树科技”）、北京泛界智能科技有限公司（“泛界智能”）签署协议，共同新设一家合营企业。目前相关经营者集中简易案件已进入公示期，公示期为 2026 年 11 月 4 日至 11 月 13 日。公示信息显示，合营企业拟从事工业具身智能机器人解决方案业务。交易后，昆仑制造及其一致行动人持有合营企业 60% 股份，宇树科技、泛界智能各自持有合营企业 20% 股份。昆仑制造、宇树科技、泛界智能将共同控制合营企业。IT之家注：昆仑制造于 2023 年 10 月 20 日于河北省雄安新区注册成立，主要从事能源装备制造业务。昆仑制造的最终控制人为中国石油天然气集团有限公司，主要从事油气业务、工程技术服务、石油工程建设等业务。在此前宇树科技科创板 IPO 的战略配售中，中国石油旗下昆仑资本便已作为重要投资方入局，占当次公开发行股份数量的 2.23%。双方已签署《战略合作备忘录》，明确围绕油气场景机器人应用展开合作。

articles.title: 利用 AI 生成涉军虚假信息等，国家网信办发布违法违规涉军“自媒体”账号典型案例
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，“网信中国”微信公众号今日发布通报，公开了一批违法违规涉军“自媒体”账号典型案例。据称，网络平台近期出现多类涉军领域违法违规有害信息，扰乱网络传播秩序，损害军队军人形象。军地职能部门依法依规关闭一批问题严重的账号。IT之家附部分典型案例通报如下：一、利用 AI 生成涉军虚假信息。网络账号“cheems 蛋仔”、“cheems 猴哥”等利用 AI 批量捏造“纠察被报复”、“新兵打架打赢就没事”等负面涉军动漫，误导网民认知。网络账号“桂 L298D8 安度晚年《冯伯爵》”等利用 AI 生成与“将军”合照，炮制不实短视频吸睛引流。网络账号“皮卡丘看好片”等制作“军区司令在私立学校被围堵”等 AI 恶搞短剧，抹黑军队形象。二、虚假宣传违规开展“军考”培训。网络账号“白白”发布“武警某战士在机构培训下军考第一”等不实营销内容，借机招揽考生牟利。网络账号“军考学堂”等声称拥有军队内部考试名额、可放宽体检标准、保上岸等，涉嫌虚假宣传和网络诈骗。三、恶意蹭涉军流量营销牟利。网络账号“半山书房”、“任宏书画艺术”等兜售所谓“将军字画”，贴蹭涉军元素招摇撞骗。网络账号“兵行者”、“干事在线”、“兵转问题咨询处理”等借转业安置话题提供有偿咨询服务，打着“内部消息”、“资深老兵解读”等噱头，诱导用户私信付费。网络账号“姚妹创业”着仿制军服蹭流量进行网络营销。网络账号“军文渠道”、“军校学历认证 vip”等散布“售卖军队文职岗位”、“代办军校学历认证”等虚假信息。四、打着退役军人旗号炒作负面信息。网络账号“橙熟”、“少吃多练”等发布服役期间演习演训敏感信息，存在失泄密风险。网络账号“退伍军人老赵”、“森”发布“军人职业前景惨淡”等不实内容，网络账号“兵途规划 — 老兵指路”发布“避坑军校”等涉军负面帖文。网络账号“孙大美戎装悟道”发布“退役后战士转道士”变装视频，以对比玩梗诋毁军旅经历。五、违规售卖军品及军用仿制品。网络账号“暖阳漫游的秘密树洞”、“行走的诸神”、“李凝幽居”在线售卖军队内部教材，存在失泄密风险。网络账号“武协调”、“徐班长的申领车”打着“内部申领”等旗号线上售卖军服被装。网络账号“黑色贝雷帽”、“无悔军旅”、“小罗拥军爱国”等假借“军工品质”、“军队记忆”名义，兜售“军用纪念品”，违反军品管理制度。

articles.title: 微软 GitHub 副总裁开源“GPU 任务管理器”工具，让显卡占用一目了然
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，微软资深开发者、微软与 GitHub 副总裁斯科特 · 汉塞尔曼（Scott Hanselman）最新发布名为 gputaskman 的开源 GPU 监控工具，帮助用户看清究竟是哪个程序在“吃”显卡资源。汉塞尔曼长期活跃于 .NET、开源、开发者社区和 AI 开发工具领域，拥有 30 多年的编程经验，曾在 Intel、Nike、STEP Technology 等公司工作，目前在 Microsoft / GitHub 担任副总裁兼技术成员。IT之家曾于今年 4 月报道，汉塞尔曼推出 PeekDesktop 工具，成功将 macOS Sonoma 系统的“点击壁纸显示桌面”功能移植到 Windows 10 和 Windows 11 平台。科技媒体 NeoWin 指出，长期以来 Windows 任务管理器虽能显示 GPU 使用率、温度等总体数据，也能在“详细信息”页开启按进程查看显存，却难以解释各进程具体在做什么。英伟达的 GPU 活动监视器同样只列出正在占用显卡的程序，信息仍较有限。gputaskman 试图补上这一缺口。gputaskman 工具可按进程展示 GPU 使用率、显存占用、温度、功耗、时钟频率、编码器与解码器活动以及 PCIe 流量等数据。对于正在本地运行大语言模型的用户，它还能识别 LLM 进程，并显示模型、运行时、模型权重、量化方式、层数和显存占用等细节，便于判断本地 AI 任务对显卡的真实压力。gputaskman 目前仍属于早期实验性软件，支持 Windows、Linux、WSL 和 Apple Silicon Mac。有试用者发现，GPU 温度偶尔会长时间停留在同一数值，未能正常刷新；开发者也提示用户实际体验可能因硬件和平台而异。参考点此前往 GitHub 访问 gputaskman 项目

articles.title: 大普微推出 M.2 形态 J5101 固态硬盘：企业级启动盘，空闲功耗 2W
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，大普微 (DapuStor) 今日宣布推出采用 M.2 2280 外形规格 J5101 NVMe 固态硬盘。这是一款 PCIe Gen4 接口的企业级启动盘，空闲功耗低至 2W，工作功耗 4.5~6.5W。J5101 M.2 基于大普微自研 DP600 主控，提供 480GB / 960GB / 1.92TB 三种容量版本。其具有 1DWPD 的写入耐久，顺序读取可达 3800MB/s，4KB 随机读取可达 650K IOPS。其支持掉电保护 (PLP) 和端到端 (E2E) 数据保护，降低数据丢失风险；支持 Secure Boot、固件安全校验，保障启动与固件安全。

articles.title: 任天堂高管称新作与重制版同等重要，经典游戏有望继续重制
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，任天堂北美产品开发与发行高级副总裁 Nate Bihldorff 在接受 Polygon 采访时表示，在任天堂的产品阵容中，全新作品与经典重制版具有“同等重要的地位”。Bihldorff 表示：“坦白讲，我认为全新作品与经典重制在任天堂的产品阵容中各有一席之地，两者的地位同等重要。我们旗下的每一个 IP 都拥有忠实粉丝。当然，能迎来这些系列的正统续作固然非常棒，我也和大家一样对此充满期待；但重温那些极其特别的经典作品（例如《时之笛》），同样能带来深层次的满足感。”该媒体表示，从 Bihldorff 的这番表态来看，任天堂在推出《塞尔达传说：时之笛》重制版后，并未停下重制经典 IP 的脚步。据IT之家此前报道，任天堂《塞尔达传说：时之笛 重制版》昨日正式发售，是这部 1998 年 N64 作品继 3DS 版之后的第二次完整高规格重制版。媒体评测已于发售前解禁。截至发稿，OpenCritic 收录 47 篇评测，均分 95；Metacritic 收录 85 家媒体评分，均分 96（截至目前的今年最高分），并获得“必玩游戏”认证。IGN 给出 9/10，评价其将经典地牢设计与系列新作的动作手感、画面表现融为一体。相关阅读：《任天堂 2027 财年半年报归母净利润 2209.17 亿日元，同比增长 11%》《任天堂 Switch 2 出货量同比下降 41%，但游戏软件销量同比增长 26%》《任天堂〈塞尔达传说：时之笛〉重制版媒体评测解禁：M 站均分 96 分成今年评分最高游戏》《任天堂〈塞尔达传说：时之笛重制版〉今日登陆 Switch 2：港区售价 449 港币》

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，比亚迪仰望汽车官方微博今日宣布，仰望 U9X 阿布扎比公共道路极速挑战，以 503.17km/h 的成绩再创全球极速新纪录。官方预热海报宣称仰望 U9X 是“地表最快量产车”。仰望汽车官方刚刚发布了 V-box 一镜到底视频，记录了仰望 U9X 阿布扎比公共道路极速挑战的全过程。大家可以跟随车手第一视角，亲历 500km/h 之上极速，感受中国超跑的突破时刻。IT之家注：在比亚迪仰望汽车官方一镜到底视频中，约 1:59 处可以捕捉到 503.17km/h 这一由中国汽车创造的全球极速新纪录。据IT之家此前报道，2025 年 9 月，比亚迪仰望 U9 Xtreme 赛道版迎来全球首秀，官方公布了这款超跑的极速成绩：德国 ATP 测试场官方认证成绩 496.22km/h，取得“无定语”的世界第一。该车全球限量 30 台。官方表示，其目标达到全球电车极速 & 圈速双第一。

articles.title: Take-Two CEO 称《GTA6》被盗版不可避免，必要时将采取法律与技术手段应对
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，《GTA6》将于 2026 年 11 月 19 日正式发售，PS5 主机破解社区近期变得越来越活跃。Take-Two 董事长兼 CEO 施特劳斯 · 泽尔尼克表示，游戏盗版始终是公司需要面对的问题，如果盗版问题变得很严重，他们将采取法律和技术手段应对。IT之家注意到，泽尔尼克认为《GTA6》被盗版是现实中不可避免的事情。不过游戏相比电影、音乐受到的影响较小，因为游戏这种载体文件更大、内容更复杂，且玩家需要连接 Take-Two 服务器才能获得完全体验。他解释称：“我曾经涉足过所有娱乐行业。在电影行业时，我们估计任何时候都有 10%-20% 内容遭到盗版。至于唱片行业，我在 1994 年至 2000 年期间曾从事过。到了 2000 年代中期，我认为市场上有 80% 内容都是盗版的。不过这些比例现在已经大幅下降。”这名 CEO 并没有否认盗版带来的问题，他认为盗版如果真的变成麻烦，Take-Two 就会用法律和技术手段解决它。

articles.title: Formalizing inverse problems in the age of AI: possibilities, pitfalls, and an invitation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06962v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Proof assistants such as Lean check mathematical proofs down to the axioms, and AI agents have recently made writing such proofs cheap. We describe AutoIP, a Lean library in which classical linear regularization theory, together with the functional analysis it rests on, has been autoformalized by AI agents. A machine-checked proof certifies only the formal statement it proves, so the remaining human task is to confirm that each formal statement says what was intended. We organize the library around this task: a reviewer compares the formal statements with their natural-language counterparts and never needs to read a proof. Our experience is that the risks lie in the statements rather than in the proofs, and that simple automated tests on the statements can expose problems even in the established literature. articles.title: Resource-Efficient Reinforcement Learning Post-Training through Elastic Expert Parallelism
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06984v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning post-training improves the capabilities of large language models, but generating training responses is a major computational bottleneck. In mixture-of-experts models, workers that finish their assigned responses may remain occupied because their experts are still needed by workers processing longer responses. Consequently, approximately one-third of occupied worker time in the baseline occurs after local response generation finishes. Here we present FlexFloor, a system that enables earlier resource release during synchronous response generation while preserving the expert computation required by ongoing responses. FlexFloor jointly adapts response scheduling and the active group of workers. It uses historical response lengths and memory constraints to guide batching and prompt placement, then progressively releases workers while maintaining expert availability and correct communication. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06989v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprises run business transactions through multi-agent AI systems spanning clouds, large language models (LLMs), orchestration harnesses, and systems of record. Finance receives AI cost only at settlement grain, aggregated by SKU and charge period. The business question (what did this order, claim, or case cost in AI?) cannot be answered from billing data, because providers never see enterprise transaction boundaries. The FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS) gives billing data one schema across providers but remains settlement-grain even as it adds AI token and requester attribution. We formalize this grain mismatch, derive seven requirements, and propose the Two-Ledger Model: a settlement ledger of FOCUS-conformant billing data joined to an attribution ledger of invocation-grain usage records built on OpenTelemetry GenAI telemetry. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have ushered in a new age of proof abundance, but helping humans understand these proofs requires new attention to the differences in how AI agents and humans pursue a proof-making task. articles.title: Trust Responsive Runtime Authorization for Agentic AI with Empirical Characterization of Policy Behavior and Parameter Sensitivity
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06996v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The policy that converts runtime estimates of an autonomous agent's condition into operational authority is rarely specified or measured. We empirically characterize the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP), which maps an Authorization Readiness Score (ARS), a weighted combination of runtime trust, operational stability, and contextual risk, onto discrete authorization levels through an asymmetric rule: escalation requires consecutive observations above a band edge plus a margin, while a sharp drop in readiness restricts authority at once. On one matched set of 100 Monte Carlo traces, we compare TRAP with static, trust-only, risk-only, and symmetric policies. articles.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07048v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evolution has shaped intelligence for billions of years. Artificial intelligence (AI) now raises a striking possibility: intelligence may begin to direct its own evolution. As AI agents become capable of modifying and evaluating their own behavior, how quickly could they improve, and how can that improvement remain safe? We develop a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution following environmental change. Darwinian evolution relies on natural selection, Lamarckian evolution adds inherited learning, and agent-directed evolution allows agents to generate and evaluate behavioral variants and choose how extensively to search. When learning is sufficiently effective, these mechanisms exhibit progressively faster adaptation. articles.title: Closed-Loop Agent Evaluation: Layered Measurement and Self-Calibration
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07051v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Once an agent is live, teams want to know whether it is doing its job, not just whether it throws errors. Yet most evaluation is one-off: a benchmark run, a look at traces, a single score. Its conclusions neither check themselves nor reach the agent. We propose closed-loop evaluation, an evaluation method for deployed agents. It models evaluation as performance estimation under biased raters and censored outcomes, and it requires every level's conclusion to trace back to atomic data and to be computed by versioned rules. The method covers four levels of analysis (span, trace, conversation and engagement), measures along a spine of Execution, Substance, Trajectory and Results, treats Conduct as a constraint throughout, and uses Provenance and Adjudication components to certify the evidence and the evaluators. articles.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07066v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Discovering cooperative behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is challenging due to the combinatorial complexity of joint state-action spaces, which hinders the emergence of coordinated behaviors from trial-and-error alone. Intrinsic rewards are often used to aid discovery, but naively combining them with team objectives can distort the learning signal, compromising task performance. In this paper, we propose EFXPLORER, a constrained exploration framework that maximizes exploration objectives subject to a constraint that preserves established task performance. We solve the resulting problem using an epigraph reformulation that introduces adaptive exploration budgets. This approach separates intrinsic rewards from task objectives and regulates exploration through task feasibility. articles.title: When Verification Is Not Agreement: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07073v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A verified Dafny postcondition certifies that a formula holds, but it does not guarantee that the result was reached through genuine independent reasoning. We introduce a cross-agent formalization protocol where a Specifier model translates clinical trial criteria into a Dafny predicate, and an Implementer model writes an operational method checked against it. A same-model control establishes that even with no capability gap, independent re-extraction from identical text agrees only 59.3% of the time. Evaluating four model configurations on 96 clinical trial documents, we find that agreement is highly sensitive to how model capability is allocated across the two roles: the GPT-4.1-nano/GPT-4.1-mini configuration achieves 53.0% agreement when the stronger model is the Implementer, but only 14.3% when the roles are reversed. articles.title: Synthesizing symbolic models of human and machine reasoning at scale
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07088v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic models offer a powerful account of cognition, but their scope has historically been limited by the need for hand-engineering and computational tractability. We show how advances in artificial intelligence (AI) can scale symbolic modeling and help overcome these engineering limitations. We introduce Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS)---an approach for automated search of interpretable, deterministic symbolic programs that verifiably reproduce behavior---and apply it to model both human and machine behavior across hundreds of challenging reasoning problems. Analyzing these programs reveals that both people and machines tend to oversimplify, adopt rules that are partial explanations for their observations, and misinfer dependencies between problem features. These shared signatures are modulated by available resources, with reasoning effort predicting the extent to which machines simplify and explain their observations.

articles.title: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for evaluating the behavior of chatbots and other AI systems. In deployment, however, their agreement with the intended human evaluation policy may degrade as user interactions and score distributions change. Existing automatic prompt optimization methods are primarily studied as one-shot procedures on static development sets and therefore provide limited guidance for maintaining LLM judges over time. We frame this problem as judge drift and introduce PromptOps, a closedloop framework for monitoring and iteratively recalibrating LLM-as-a-Judge (LLMaaJ) systems. PromptOps separates four operational decisions: when to optimize, which optimization procedure to apply, which feedback records to use, and how to update the judge prompt. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Power matters for AI safety. Optimal agents tend to acquire power across a wide range of objectives (instrumental convergence). As we embed AI agents into socio-technical systems, humans risk gradual disempowerment. Both concerns call for a formal, quantitative measure of power. Two such measures in the context of Markov games are information-theoretic empowerment, the capacity of the channel from an agent's actions to future states, and capability-based individual power, a measure of goal attainment built from the probabilities that a human would attain each goal in a family of candidates were they pursuing it. We show where the two meet. From individual power, Fano's inequality yields a floor $B(s)$. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When a tropical cyclone (TC) threatens several ports, preparedness planning depends on anticipating which ports are likely to be affected and where disruptions may last longest. Limited historical observations at individual ports and uncertainty in landfall location make these relative impacts difficult to estimate. We use a two-stage recommendation framework that first selects candidate ports based on their proximity to the expected landfall location and then ranks them by their estimated number of impact days. Using AIS-derived impact days for 37 ports and 31 TCs in the Gulf of Mexico study region, we compare three ways of representing port--cyclone interactions: pairwise feature interactions, tree-based feature combinations, and explicit feature crosses combined with learned embeddings. articles.title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07372v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An LLM agent's cost and success depend on its model, its harness, and its environment. In addition to the widely studied directions of parameter tuning and harness optimization, we propose the third direction: optimization over stationary environments. Agents are often deployed in rich environments shared by many tasks, such as a company's Slack workspace or a complex collection of data sources, documents or tickets. We call these environments stationary environments. We introduce EnvOpt, a method for automated end-to-end optimization of stationary environments for any given model and harness, using real or synthetic tasks without needing any graders or reference answers. On AutomationBench, EnvOpt reduces the cost of Claude Haiku 4.5 by 72.7% and raises its pass rate by 14.34%. The same environment transfers to Opus 5, cutting its cost by 68.1% with a 1.34% gain. articles.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07464v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language agents increasingly work for users on the open Web, and finance is where trusting them is hardest. The data must come from the Web, the strategy lives in the user's head, and correctness depends on time, so an agent can fail silently: a strategy the user never asked for, unverified data, or a backtest that uses the future yields a report as convincing as a correct one. Existing benchmarks close the world somewhere, fixing the task, the data, or the timeline, and thereby remove these failures instead of measuring them. We introduce FINCOSMOS, an open-world evaluation paradigm for agents doing financial work. A simulated user holds a hidden strategy sampled from a compositional grammar and reveals it only when asked. The agent receives no data, so it must acquire data from the Web, build its own backtest under a data cutoff, and deliver verifiable results. Grading needs no reference answer. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07482v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have achieved impressive performance via explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, yet this process introduces critical safety risks. We formalize LRM safety objectives as requiring non-malicious reasoning and answers, safety consistency, and explicit intent identification. We argue that existing alignment methods suffer from poor adversarial generalization, a significant ``safety tax'' on reasoning, and unfaithful coarse-grained rewards, primarily due to their neglect of the LRM's intrinsic reasoning capabilities for safety. To address these, we propose \textbf{SAVeR$^2$}, a novel \textbf{S}afety \textbf{A}lignment method via \textbf{R}ewards with \textbf{R}easoning capability. SAVeR$^2$ decomposes the safety objective into four fine-grained verifiable reward signals and utilizes a difficulty-aware data selection strategy to stabilize training. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07508v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents that work for an individual over time may also help that individual serve external clients. We define a personal external service agent as an agent authorized and continuously managed by a specific individual to accept client requests, deliver work, and provide ongoing support using that person's knowledge, experience, professional methods, and service boundaries. Such agents could allow individuals to serve more clients with less direct involvement and generate economic value at scale. We propose DelegateEval, a platform-level evaluation framework for agent systems that may combine large language models, reusable skills, protocols such as MCP, and executable tool environments. articles.title: Graph learning-assisted logic-based Benders decomposition for distributionally robust in-station train rescheduling under disruptions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07520v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Uncertainty in resource reopening times complicates train holding and rerouting decisions when resource closures coincide with arrival delays and processing-time extensions. We develop a rolling-horizon distributionally robust model that updates predictions of the remaining closure duration as observations of disruption resolution become available. The model jointly optimizes train routes, sequences, and timings. It minimizes the worst-case expected total completion delay over an ambiguity set of scenario probabilities. The solution algorithm, GNN-LBBD, uses logic-based Benders decomposition to coordinate routing and resource scheduling. Conditional cuts are constructed from resource-use patterns, and a graph neural network guides the order in which resource relaxation subproblems are solved. articles.content:

Abstract: Steel property models can perform well on random test splits even when they extrapolate poorly to unfamiliar alloys. SteelAgent couples metallurgical descriptors and machine-learning models with a language-model interface for property prediction, uncertainty reporting and inverse design. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06979v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: M/EEG source imaging requires accurate localization and reliable uncertainty estimates, yet posterior credible regions are rarely assessed for empirical calibration. We present a simulation-based framework for uncertainty quantification and calibration of empirical Bayesian inverse methods with closed-form conditional Gaussian posterior summaries. We compare Bayesian minimum norm (BMN) with sLORETA depth weighting and sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) with sparse basis field expansions (S-FLEX). S-FLEX allows retained coefficients to contribute nonzero marginal posterior variance at locations where voxel-wise SBL yields degenerate variances. For BMN, we derive joint source- and noise-variance updates through evidence maximization. We test whether adaptive noise learning yields near-calibrated uncertainties. Abstract: Data Streams are characterised as a potentially infinite source of data subject to non-stationarity. articles.title: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07025v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoregressive decoding relies on the KV cache, whose memory footprint grows linearly with context length and caps batch size and throughput. Existing post-training methods exploit redundancy across tokens, layers, and feature dimensions, or lower numerical precision. We identify a complementary axis: within each attention head, values are largely predictable from their corresponding keys. We exploit this with value cache amortisation, which fits a lightweight per-head predictor at test time and stores residuals only for the tokens it reconstructs worst, giving $4\times$ near-lossless value compression. The predictor can be initialised by meta-learning for substantially reduced prefill overhead, or fitted from scratch in settings that allow a one-off cost, such as multi-query inference. articles.title: Stochastic Dynamics of Generative AI: From Autoregressive Models to Interacting LLM Networks and Neural SDEs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07065v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper develops a stochastic dynamical-systems perspective on three classes of generative AI models. First, we formulate large language models (LLMs) as high-dimensional nonlinear autoregressive models with attention-based dependencies. This formulation connects pretraining by conditional maximum likelihood to sequential token generation and provides a probabilistic interpretation of LLM operation. Second, we consider networks of interacting LLMs and characterize their collective behavior through mean-field ordinary differential equations. These dynamics provide a framework for understanding emergent preferential attachment and persistent structural biases, including type-dependent glass-ceiling effects. Third, we consider neural stochastic differential equations (SDEs) as continuous-time generative models for stochastic trajectories, including those observed at irregular time intervals. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07069v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) in Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) is computationally challenging due to the curse of long-range dependence on history. Fortunately, recent studies have shown that a range of POMDPs that satisfy the filter stability assumption can be well approximated by a superstate Markov Decision Process (MDP) based on a truncated history in a finite-memory window, with a value gap that decays with the window length. However, existing finite-time convergence analyses on such superstate MDP surrogates are either limited to over-simplified linear function approximation or rely on an i.i.d. sampling oracle that is violated by POMDP trajectories, both of which severely limit the applicability of these theoretical results in practice. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07071v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose Mechanistic Shaping, a unified framework for shaping models through their internal representations. Mechanistic Shaping is applied during training so that models follow specifications (rules) about which concepts they express, measured via their outputs or internal representations (e.g., no harmful content), and also which concepts they rely on, i.e., what they use to make their decisions (e.g., not a candidate's gender when screening a r\'esum\'e). articles.title: Optimistic Hedge in General-Sum Games: Fundamental Limits and Regret Bounds via Temporal Approximation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07078v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Optimistic Hedge, a multiplicative weight update with one step of extrapolation, is one of the most natural regret-minimizing dynamics for games, and characterizing its regret has been a longstanding open question. Daskalakis, Fishelson and Golowich proved that if all $m$ players in a finite general-sum game follow Optimistic Hedge with a fixed learning rate, each player's regret is polylogarithmic in the horizon $T$. Subsequently, Ha showed that an appropriate choice of learning rate makes each player's regret bounded independently of $T$. This bound, however, is non-constructive and its dependence on the number of actions $n$ is not explicit, leaving open whether Optimistic Hedge can achieve a constant regret bound which is polynomial in the size of the game.
  We show that the answer hinges on the number of players. In two-player games, there is a learning rate for which Optimistic Hedge guarantees $O(n\log n)$ regret independent of t

articles.title: Server-Side Sparse Assignment for Federated Mixture-of-Experts
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07093v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly recognized for their remarkable capabilities; federated learning (FL) offers a promising framework for collaboratively fine-tuning LLMs on edge devices while achieving data privacy. However, edge devices are inherently heterogeneous: clients may exhibit diverse data distributions and resource constraints, including limited memory and computation budgets. Recent federated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches address these challenges by using sparse expert activation or partial expert loading. However, existing partial-expert methods rely on heuristic full-pool observations or prioritize system-wide load balance, without guarantees for recovering client-specific relevant experts from partial observations. Abstract: A challenge to Weight Space Learning as it expands from task specific and vision models to Large Language Models (LLMs) is the absence of a well curated and analyzed LLM population. articles.title: Regulating Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand Operators with Fixed and Adaptive Penalties: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07122v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Profit-maximizing Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand (AMoD) operators may exploit consumer surplus through excessive prices and underserve less profitable regions by relocating vehicles away from them. We study how penalty-based regulation of an AMoD operator in a multimodal mobility system can limit surge pricing and improve regional service availability. We model regulation as an outer control loop that acts on a learning-based operator. Static regulation with fixed penalties is formulated as a Markov Decision Process for an operator that jointly controls pricing and rebalancing, and dynamic regulation as a Partially Observable Stochastic Game in which a regulator periodically adjusts region-specific penalties in closed loop. Operator and regulator policies are learned with graph-based multi-agent reinforcement learning. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07124v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine-learning models predicting live birth after in vitro fertilisation (IVF) or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) from routine clinical data report performance from near chance to near perfect. We systematically reviewed these models under PRISMA 2020, searching OpenAlex, Scopus and Web of Science to 22 October 2026, appraised them with PROBAST+AI and TRIPOD+AI, and pooled their discrimination with random-effects meta-analysis on the logit scale. Models evaluated only internally pooled to an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.814, against 0.756 (95% prediction interval 0.546-0.889) for models evaluated on a later period or another centre, and 0.764 for studies not at high risk of bias; neither differenc

articles.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07125v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Molten chloride corrosion has been studied for decades, yet reliable prediction across different alloys, salts, and test conditions remains difficult. In this work, 291 static molten chloride corrosion experiments reported in the literature were compiled into a structured dataset and used to develop an interpretable machine-learning framework for corrosion-rate predictions. To better represent the differences in salt condition across studies, a Chloride Salt Preparation Index (CSPI) was introduced to bring the reported salt-treatment method, atmosphere control, and pre-exposure impurity condition on a common numerical scale. A blended tree-based ensemble provided the most consistent predictive performance, achieving a cross-validated \(R^2\) of 0.85 and an MAE of 0.41 mg cm\(^{-2}\) day\(^{-1}\). The graded CSPI retained more useful information than a simple purified/unpurified classification and emerged as the dominant model descriptor.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07127v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reliable uncertainty quantification is essential for clinical deployment of cancer diagnosis models, yet neural networks and variational Gaussian process methods can produce overconfident predictions, particularly under the distribution shifts that arise when models trained at one hospital are applied at another. This makes HMC posterior sampling in the low-rank latent representation tractable at N approximately 300,000 training points, enabling HC-based low-rank GPC on substantially larger datasets than prior MCMC-based demonstrations. articles.title: Teaching Agents the "Principle", Not the "Reward"
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07130v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning has achieved strong performance in many tasks by letting agents learn from nothing more than a reward signal. However, in more complex tasks, agents still struggle to learn good, generalizable policies, even with carefully designed rewards and abundant samples. We argue that this difficulty stems from the reward decoding burden: designers encode their knowledge of the desired behavior into rewards and penalties, and agents must infer this knowledge from long sequences of noisy scalars. To address this burden, we propose prescriptive policy learning (PPL), which directly teaches agents higher-level knowledge about the tasks, termed principles of behavior, such as how to maintain balance, how to accumulate energy, and how to land smoothly. Through appropriately selected key quantities and references, PPL can directly indicate at every step whether the agent follows the principles and to what extent. Our experiments s

articles.title: Depth or Description? When a One-Step Latent Score Replaces Lookahead in Proactive Information Acquisition
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07155v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A proactive agent must decide what to ask before it acts. Exact lookahead values combinations of questions but is expensive and leans on a fitted model; a one-step score is cheap but can miss them. Our main finding: the need for depth often lies in how the hidden cause is described. A one-step score on the label can be blind to an interaction among answers. A score on a suitable latent cause is not, and where that latent encodes the decision it replaces most of depth at a fraction of the search. Described differently, the same problem can defeat the score while exact values do not move, so keep the latent small and check it against exact values. Probabilities learned from one language model's answers do not carry to another unless planning allows for both; those read from tokens are worth only a few labels.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07160v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many real-world applications, such as numerical weather prediction or wildfire tracking, involve modeling highly nonlinear dynamical systems that are chaotic and influenced by various sources of uncertainty. To improve model prediction accuracy and reduce such uncertainties, data assimilation (DA) combines the dynamical model with partial, noisy observations to estimate the evolution of the system's state. Doing so depends on solving the optimal filtering problem: computing the conditional distribution of a hidden state given a sequence of observations. articles.title: Structural Conditional Independence Test via Neural Quantile Resolution
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conditional independence testing is difficult when dependence is weak, localized, or expressed through distributional changes rather than a global mean shift. Existing tests usually return a scalar statistic or p-value, which summarizes evidence against independence but does not describe where the conditional law changes. We propose QRCIT, a quantile-resolution conditional independence test that compares P(X|Z) and P(X|Y,Z) through a quantile deformation learned by a shared model. A lightweight residual quantile-flow model first learns the baseline conditional quantile law and then learns the additional deformation induced by Y, yielding a global predictive-gain statistic with conditional-randomization calibration and an inspectable deformation field over context and quantile level. articles.title: Interactive Backdoor Attacks in LLM-Based Proactive Dialogue Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06969v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based proactive dialogue systems provide goal-directed support through sustained interaction. Fine-tuning their underlying models on externally supplied dialogue data introduces backdoor risks. Existing LLM backdoor studies primarily focus on eliciting an attacker-specified response upon trigger activation. We present an interactive backdoor attack framework that uses training-data poisoning to steer post-trigger, multi-turn interactions toward an attacker-specified objective. Poisoned fine-tuning dialogues implant a trigger-conditioned guidance-policy bias that ordinary user utterances can activate, without deployment-time prompt modification or further attacker intervention. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06976v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer (PACT), a form of latent communication between language models, combines a larger model's prompt representations with a smaller model's efficient generation, offering a promising way to balance capability and inference cost. However, existing systems provide limited support for independently evaluating large-small model collaboration, and improved task performance alone does not establish whether the receiver benefits from the sender's information. We introduce PLatour, an open-source PACT framework that connects frozen models through lightweight, zero-initialized linear bridges trained directly with task rewards and supports hybrid-attention architectures. PLatour significantly outperforms open-source baselines on generation tasks and surpasses Mostik's reported results on shared mathematics and coding benchmarks using a substantially smaller sender. articles.title: Follow the Policy, Fail the Benchmark: Auditing and Revising Policy-Based Decision Benchmarks
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07042v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Policy-based decision benchmarks evaluate whether systems apply written rules to financial and operational cases. Yet a rule-following response can be marked wrong when the benchmark misstates the required decision. We audit nine public policy-based decision benchmarks through source tracing, program execution, and controlled checks. We find unsupported targets, reference errors that survive replay or propagate as solved steps, and evaluators that reject acceptable answers or credit incomplete decisions. To measure the scoring impact, we rescore unchanged model responses. On the 96 LegalBench SARA numeric cases, correcting the scorer raises acceptance by more than 80 percentage points for each of three models, without changing references or responses. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07054v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Genetic variants are routinely reclassified in ClinVar after a patient is tested, sometimes from uncertain to pathogenic, yet patient recontact is inconsistent, with no clear duty and responsibility diffused among labs, providers, and patients. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07072v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated feedback on classroom discourse improves instruction in professional and online teaching contexts, and recent work suggests that delivering similar feedback to learners may strengthen these effects by sharing responsibility for participation. Whether this holds in small-group volunteer tutoring has not been tested. We present results from a randomized controlled trial across two four-week SAT mathematics bootcamps on the Schoolhouse.world platform, involving 1,030 volunteer tutors, 7,443 learners and 6,508 recorded sessions. Tutors were randomly assigned to receive no feedback, automated feedback on their own discourse, or that feedback together with participation feedback delivered to their learners under one of two motivational framings. articles.title: Consistent yet Contextual: Learning Author-Level Mixtures of Style for Authorship Attribution
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07111v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Approaches to authorship verification or attribution typically model the style of a document, asking whether two documents were likely written by the same author. While recent approaches have been performant, such approaches largely ignore modeling the authors themselves and how varied their style is. Here, we introduce multiple alternatives for modeling the author and demonstrate that allowing an author's representation to capture multiple consistent but distinct writing styles yields significant performance improvements. Using our new authorship model, we then examine when an author writes in a way that is most idiomatic of their style across four scenarios: (i) variation in the size of their writing audiences, (ii) temporal distance from when the model was trained, (iii) the effect of preceding context, and (iv) the effect of genre norms on style. articles.title: What Patients Say They Can't Access: Mining Cancer Screening Barriers from Online Communities
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07113v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cancer screening disparities persist across the U.S., yet the patient-reported barriers driving low uptake remain poorly characterized at scale. While clinical surveys capture structured responses, they miss the organic, unsolicited discourse where patients candidly describe real-world obstacles. In this paper, we conduct a large-scale analysis of over 56,000 posts across six cancer-specific Reddit communities to surface barriers to cancer screening among U.S. patients. We apply a pipeline combining keyword filtering, barrier triage, open coding, and codebook synthesis to systematically extract and categorize patient-reported barriers from 576 U.S.-located posts. Our qualitative analysis reveals recurring structural, informational, and psychosocial barriers that vary meaningfully by cancer type and community context. These findings lay the groundwork for future work aimed at proactively identifying and addressing barriers at scale - span

articles.title: Adapting LLM Judges to Observed Human Annotation Policy through Soft Prompt Tuning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07126v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly employed as automated judges for evaluating chatbot responses. While proprietary models can achieve high agreement with human annotators, they remain costly and difficult to deploy in practical settings. Lightweight open-source LLM judges provide an attractive alternative but typically exhibit lower agreement with human ratings. In this paper, we investigate whether soft prompt tuning can align open-source LLM judges more closely with human annotation policy. We train soft prompts on the FairBotBench benchmark and evaluate the adapted judges across the dimensions of bias, toxicity, and personalization. Our findings demonstrate that hybrid soft-prompt tuning, which combines textual prompts with learned continuous prompt embeddings, consistently improves agreement with human annotations over the corresponding untuned baselines. articles.title: Matriarchy Classics: A Computational Approach to Swap Only Gendered Words in Classic Novels
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07134v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper proposes a trustworthy computational method to gender-swap public domain novels, with programmatic guarantees that only gendered words are inverted and all other words are left unchanged. This may seem like a simple task, but both large language models and naive rule-based methods fail to complete it. The proposed method includes a custom whitespace-preserving tokenizer, gender-swap mappings across plural and possessive forms, pronoun handling, and a character renaming strategy. It shortens the time required to gender-swap a novel from weeks of manual labor to minutes. The method is demonstrated on two public-domain novels. Pride and Prejudice is transported to matriarchal Regency England, where inheritance flows through daughters, mothers rule the household, and a frantic Mr. Bennet is determined to secure advantageous marriages for his sons. articles.title: {\tau}-bench-LILT: Evaluating Conversational Agents on Realistic Multilingual Tool-Use Tasks
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07203v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frontier evaluations of tool-using conversational agents are conducted almost exclusively in English, leaving a critical gap for organizations deploying agents in other languages and regions. We present ${\tau}$-bench-LILT, a multilingual extension of ${\tau^3}$-bench covering German, Korean, Turkish, and Farsi in the airline, retail, telecom, and banking domains. We natively localize every layer of the benchmark: customer databases are populated with culturally appropriate records, user-simulator prompts are refined iteratively through contrastive annotation by native-language experts, and tasks are updated according to the localized database and to reflect realistic tasks in the target region. Evaluation across eight agent models shows the largest drops compared to English in the Korean and Farsi retail domains, by up to 61 points in pass^4. Code and data released at https://github.com/lilt/tau-bench-lilt.

articles.title: SAFE-Teen: Evaluating Chatbot Safety Across Adolescent Mental Health Conversations
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07218v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adolescents are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for mental health support, advice, and companionship, raising safety concerns. While recent evaluations have started to examine safety across multiple conversational turns, few compare how slight changes in a teen's responses can affect a chatbot's safety in the same scenario. We conduct a clinician-informed evaluation of chatbot safety in simulated conversations with adolescents aged 13-17, examining how safety failures vary with adolescents' responses and teen-aware system prompting. We evaluated 32,555 simulated conversations across 18 chatbot APIs and two system-prompt conditions using 22 safety criteria grounded in previously identified harms. Conversations spanned 983 variants of 106 seed scenarios covering urgent safety issues, health advice, and identity and relationships. articles.title: Source-balanced Capped Fisher: Bounded Evidence Aggregation for User Inference in Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07228v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: User inference asks whether a source contributed documents to a language-model update, even when the auditor observes only fresh documents from that source. Document-level scores can provide evidence of participation, but combining this evidence is challenging: documents differ in baseline predictability and in how strongly they reflect information learned from other documents of the same source. We propose source-balanced capped Fisher (SCF), an aggregation method that uses known nonparticipating sources to assess how unusual each document score is. It transforms the resulting reference-tail frequencies into negative-log evidence, caps individual contributions, and averages them within each source. This limits the influence of isolated extreme scores while retaining evidence across multiple documents. articles.title: Recursive Sparse Attention: Million-Token Length Extrapolation at Logarithmic Cost
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07232v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: At context lengths of about 1M tokens, dense attention is costly in prefill and decoding, and training typically relies on long documents, which become scarcer as the target length increases. Most sparse attention methods score all preceding blocks or tokens, so their selection cost per query is $O(L)$ at context length $L$; hierarchical selection reduces it to $O(\log L)$, but prior trainable hierarchical methods report accuracy only within their training length. We propose RecSA (Recursive Sparse Attention), which builds a tree over the KV cache in which each node summarizes its subtree with one key and one mean-pooled value. The keys come from one pooler per layer, shared by all levels and distilled from dense attention. Each level above the tokens selects at most $k$ candidates, so each query has $O(\log L)$ selection cost and reads $O(\log L)$ entries; the summaries of unselected candidates share one softmax with the exact tokens. articles.title: Archetypal contexts in the neurons of language models: an architecture for intelligence?
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07234v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We validate our previous hypothesis that a language model holds relational patterns apart from the subject domains that instantiate them (Nordfors, 2026). These archetypal contexts are patterns of relations that people recognize across many fields, such as the tipping point or winner takes all, held once and applied across domains. We show this inside the model, Qwen3.8-27B. One set of neurons carries the archetype, say the tipping point; another carries the topic, say politics, ecology or cell biology; a third carries the language, such as English, Spanish or Chinese. Silence the tipping point's neurons, and the model no longer identifies the pattern but still knows what the text is about. Silence the topic's, and it loses the topic but still names the pattern. articles.title: How Do AI Agents Waste Your Money?
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07238v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents may consume massive tokens across a wide range of tasks, but how many of those tokens are really necessary? Although prior work has shown that agents can incur unexpectedly high token costs, we still lack a systematic way to identify and measure token waste. Abstract: Parallel block drafting accelerates speculative decoding by predicting multiple future positions in a single backbone pass, but on-device deployment constrains both drafter capacity and context storage. arXiv:2611.07453v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Test-time compute (TTC) improves language model responses by spending additional computation at inference time, and the right amount of compute depends on the prompt. Abstract: How can an agent handle a real-world task end to end? Frontier models with their own harnesses still fall short on real-world benchmarks: on Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex resolves 37.3% of the tasks and Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code 51.8%. These tasks fail at the step from reaching a resource to applying it, which we call the last mile to the real world. Existing approaches put the resource within reach but leave the competence to apply it with the caller, so each harness rebuilds that competence. articles.title: T$^2$-Splat: Adaptive Topology Mesh Splatting with Texture Residuals
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06974v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Triangle-based splatting connects novel view synthesis with conventional graphics pipelines, but often requires excessive tessellation to preserve appearance details. We present T$^2$-Splat, which decouples topology adaptation from appearance refinement. Safe Restricted Delaunay Triangulation (Safe RDT) initializes mesh connectivity. Dynamic Topology Evolution (DTE) then adapts triangle allocation through edge collapse and vertex split operations. Residual per-face Mip-textures then refine appearance on the fixed mesh using scale-adaptive filtering. Experiments on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and DTU demonstrate competitive results with compact meshes. T$^2$-Splat improves PSNR by 0.71dB over MeshSplatting on Mip-NeRF 360. Additional compression experiments demonstrate flexible control of mesh complexity, supporting face budgets as low as 10% of the original face count. Project page: https://t2-splat.github.io/.

Abstract: Video understanding models often rely on motion, yet their explanations can obscure which motion sources support a prediction. These concepts represent dynamic evidence from people, objects, and interactions, while object and scene concepts account for static context. Abstract: Hybrid Mesh-Gaussian rendering combines compact textured surfaces with flexible 3D Gaussian primitives, offering an efficient alternative to purely Gaussian scene representations for structured environments. Abstract: Flow matching (FM) generators often face a quality-coverage tradeoff. Inference-time techniques such as classifier-free guidance raise quality, but at the cost of coverage. Abstract: Few-shot adaptation of vision-language models must balance two competing goals: learning fine-grained visual distinctions from very limited supervision and preserving the efficiency that makes frozen CLIP-like models attractive for deployment. Existing lightweight adaptation methods, including prompt tuning, LoRA, and cache-based adapters, typically supervise global image embeddings and therefore underuse token-level structure. Abstract: Multi-perspective-camera systems are widely adopted since they provide broad visual coverage for autonomous driving, motivating the synthesis of a unified wide view from spatially separated observations. Abstract: Self-supervised learning has given rise to vision foundation models that learn general-purpose image representations transferable across downstream tasks, yet representation learning for 3D scenes has not achieved comparable success. We then redesign two core objectives of modern approaches built around student-teacher networks: matching representations across views and predicting masked content from visible context. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07188v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Radiologists read a screening mammogram by first forming a global impression of the four views and then selectively magnifying suspicious regions before assigning a BI-RADS assessment. MLLMs, in contrast, see the whole image at a fixed, reduced resolution, which makes sub-millimeter calcifications invisible, and they perform close to chance on mammography. Therefore, we present MammoSeek, a mammography agent that reproduces this reading process. After forming an impression of each breast, the agent performs selective zooming: it decides by itself which detector candidates deserve a closer look and inspects only those on full-resolution views. Guided by a BI-RADS assessment skill, it then assigns a category and generates a localized, lexicon-structured report for each breast; its assessment is combined with image-model scores in a decision layer to decide recall. Abstract: Reinforcement learning has become an effective approach for improving video generation, but its success depends heavily on reliable reward models. Abstract: Single image dehazing requires recovering scene radiance from visual responses that are weakened and veiled by participating media. articles.title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07408v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes. Abstract: Large language models understand passengers' driving commands, but as driving agents they reason in generated text for seconds and must infer each action's consequences implicitly from the scene. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05507v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humanoid motion tracking has scaled to general policies that reproduce diverse human motion, but the resulting behavior is in free-space: the tracker knows where the body should be, not how it should interact with the environment. Other work makes the object part of the objective, yet abstracts that interaction to contact or geometry, which leaves the demanding cases under-explored. We argue that force is a natural command channel between motion imitation and object interaction, one that specifies not just where to make contact but how hard. We present Ctrl-F, a hierarchical motion-force framework that augments motion tracking with an explicit force command, a 3-D force at each designated contact body such as a hand or a foot. articles.title: MESA: An Evaluation Framework for Compositional, Semantic, and Spatial Generalization in Robotics
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05567v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Despite growing interest in foundation models for robotic manipulation, systematic evaluation of their capabilities remains elusive. Existing benchmarks are either narrow and saturated, offering little signal on SOTA methods, broadly scoped, providing diversity at the cost of controlled experimentation, or require training on large, messy open-source datasets. We introduce MESA, an evaluation framework designed for precise, reproducible measurement of language-conditioned policy generalization. MESA provides five evaluation suites that isolate in-distribution performance and four distinct axes of generalization: spatial configuration, object instance, object category, and subtask composition, enabling researchers to diagnose where and why policies fail, not just whether they fail. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05571v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robot imitation learning is limited by the scarcity of action-labeled data, while action-free demonstrations such as videos are abundant. Recent latent-action methods learn action-relevant representations from observation transitions, but they do not optimize latent actions for downstream control, leading to latent representations that are difficult for policies to model and difficult to accurately decode into continuous robot actions. This paper introduces ELA, an end-to-end framework for learning from video demonstrations via latent actions jointly optimized for policy learning and action decoding. ELA jointly trains a latent action model, latent action policy, and action decoder, enabling policies to leverage abundant video data with only a handful of action-labeled robot demonstrations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05585v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This letter presents a trajectory planner for humanoid robots to perform dynamic motions on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. The planner generates feasible movements without predefined contact sequences, considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics. To plan bipedal locomotion on steps, ramps, and other terrains, we propose a mathematical model to approximate ground geometry with a smooth surface. The rigid interaction between the robot and the ground is modeled via novel contact constraints, extending the domain of applicability from flat and horizontal surfaces to any arbitrary smooth surface. Abstract: High motion performance and avoiding structural vibrations rely on smooth trajectory planning. For industrial robots, the smoothness requirements have been determined and subsequently taken into account. Although unknown for soft continuum robots, the exact smoothness requirement can potentially be much larger than previously considered ones such as $\mathbf{\mathcal{C}^4}$ for collaborative robots and $\mathbf{\mathcal{C}^5}$ for quadcopter drones. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05667v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents Proactive Human-in-the-Loop (PHIL), a framework for proactive policy correction and preference-based post-training. PHIL enables operators to preview policy-predicted future motion and intervene before anticipated undesirable actions. During takeover, PHIL continues querying the policy and displaying its predicted trajectories in the physical workspace through an extended reality (XR) interface. PHIL pairs rejected policy predictions with corrective action chunks subsequently executed from the same physical state over the same horizon, and preference-based post-training encourages the policy to favor these corrections. This paper evaluates PHIL on four real-world manipulation tasks using a diffusion policy and a pretrained vision-language-action policy. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05738v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. We introduce OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation. OdorSpaces augments Habitat-Sim with 3D odor transport and dispersion simulated by Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS), enabling agents to navigate photorealistic indoor environments using both visual and olfactory observations. The benchmark includes two representative source-seeking scenarios: invisible gas-leak localization and early-stage fire localization. articles.content:

Abstract: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. In standard bedside assessments, these stimuli are applied manually, resulting in substantial variation in force, duration, frequency, and location. Here, we present OUCH (Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic stimulation), a wrist-worn device that uses pneumatic actuation to deliver noxious mechanical stimuli. OUCH combines stacked pneumatic pouch actuators, a rigid indenter, and a compliant spacer designed to buckle at a set load, so that the indenter contacts the skin only during actuation. Abstract: We study physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations for robot learning: finding robot controls that reproduce reference motions under contact dynamics. GRASP-TO extends tempered sequential Monte Carlo by fitting local quadratic cost models to archived rollouts and using their gradients to guide Markov chain Monte Carlo rejuvenation. Abstract: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. We observe that the optimal correction is often multimodal: when a slower opponent can be passed on either side, good corrections of opposite sign coexist, and the expert's choice between them hinges on tiny cost differences. Deterministic regression then averages modes or inherits inconsistent expert tie-breaking. We propose ZipDrift, which trains a one-step drifting generator over MPC cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations of candidate corrections, without differentiating through the optimiser. Abstract: Assessing the deployment performance of learned robot policies during training is challenging, as directly measuring task success requires costly real-world trials for each candidate checkpoint. Averaged validation loss offers a rollout-free alternative, but its checkpoint rankings can be inconsistent with deployment performance. We analyze two limitations of this criterion: it penalizes action deviations without considering whether the policy can recover from them, and gives later reference predictions equal weight even when earlier deviations may lead execution away from the reference. We propose RACE, a novel rollout-free metric for ranking checkpoints using a fixed set of held-out successful trajectories. Abstract: The optimal rapidly exploring random tree (RRT*) is proven asymptotically optimal on open subsets of Euclidean space with straight-line local planning. We ask whether it works on a triangle-mesh terrain, a two-dimensional surface in R^3. Abstract: An ordered sequence of end-effector poses can give a redundant robot arm multiple valid joint configurations at each waypoint. Inverse kinematics (IK) computes these configurations. Choosing a configuration only for the next waypoint can leave the arm poorly placed for later waypoints. This may increase planned motion time or cause a later planning failure. FWIK generates several IK candidates, connects them in a layered joint-space graph, and ranks candidate paths with a simple motion-time estimate. A learned model removes paths whose transitions are likely to cause self-collision. Abstract: Off-policy deep reinforcement learning trains on random samples from a replay buffer of past experience. Abstract: Integrating six-axis tactile feedback into robotic interfaces requires compact sensors with accurate load measurement and rapid online reconstruction. This paper presents LumiTac, a low-profile, camera-free optoelectronic tactile sensor combining spatially distributed illumination with spectral encoding. A compact multilayer perceptron reconstructs three force and three moment components from 20 optical channels. Abstract: Visual-inertial odometry relies on visual features that correspond to 3D points with consistent projections across sequential frames. In reflective indoor-floor environments, however, specular floor patterns can be detected and triangulated as virtual features below the physical ground plane, producing unreliable feature associations and inconsistent visual residuals. This paper proposes a lightweight reflection-aware front-end for feature-based stereo VIO. Rather than suppressing all floor-region features, the proposed method estimates the ground height in real time and rejects only feature candidates whose inferred 3D positions are below the estimated ground height. articles.title: Learning Object-Centric Motion Priors from Human for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05979v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Manipulating diverse objects with multi-fingered dexterous hands is challenging due to the high dimensionality and complex dynamics. Human-Object Interaction (HOI) datasets provide rich knowledge about task information and embodied interactions. Instead of solely imitating the human demonstrations, our method learns to holistically predict future hand-object states by leveraging these datasets. The predicted future states of the object can serve as a general-purpose reward term for reinforcement learning, reducing reliance on task-specific reward engineering and enhancing generalization across tasks. We conduct extensive experiments on three manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world. Our approach outperforms existing SOTA methods in both success rate and generalizability on novel objects. Furthermore, we validate the cross-embodiment compatibility of our methods by successfully deploying the skills on different robot hands.

articles.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
articles.content: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. This structure is directly predicted by generative models of user behavior for linear embeddings and extends approximately to deep-learning representations by the superposition hypothesis. Superimposed modes can naturally be recovered by sparse dictionary learning methods, such as sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and recovered modes can be automatically named and queried in natural language. We validate mode recovery against known ground truth on synthetic data, where SAEs recover modes better than classical sparse baselines, including on transformer-encoded embeddings. We then apply the method to classical and transformer-based user embeddings from two real-world datasets. We also show how the corresponding natural-language labels enable zero-shot audience retrieval and characterization over embeddings never trained on text. The framework is post-hoc and model-agnostic, requiring no modification to the upstream embedding system.

articles.title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
articles.content: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. The corpus comprises a quota-based main sample of 160 papers spanning four temporal periods and a separate purposive style-contrast sample of 40 papers. A single multimodal judge evaluates six dimensions of communication and design, with three repeated judgments per figure. We attempt source-constrained revisions of all 371 figures, of which 369 pass the recorded fidelity checks. Original-figure ratings show no uniform decline across periods. Revisions increase mean clarity ratings by 0.428 points and decrease aesthetic coherence ratings by 0.111 points on a five-point scale. Gains in the six-dimension average are larger for main-sample motivation figures than for frameworks. Case analyses show that added explanation can clarify comparisons while leaving typographic hierarchy and visual economy unresolved. These model-based findings support researcher-led design, with AI assisting exploration and authors retaining responsibility for explanatory purpose, composition, and scientific relationships. The accompanying atlas and evaluation records are available at https://ntu-ai4x.github.io/Rethinking_Figures/index_en.html.

articles.title: Where and Why is Grounded Reasoning Useful?
articles.content: Grounded reasoning, where a model outputs text coordinates of relevant locations in chain-of-thought reasoning, is a common strategy for solving complex visual reasoning problems. However, the benefits and limitations of grounded reasoning are understudied. We study where and why grounded reasoning is most useful. To do so, we introduce a chain-of-thought analysis method to measure how much a model uses its outputted grounding in its thinking trace and perform a detailed ablation study of a grounded reasoning training recipe. We find that grounded reasoning improves counting but shows no significant gain over baselines without coordinate grounding across a wide range of spatial reasoning and perception benchmarks. Using several synthetic tasks, we show that grounded reasoning is most useful when a task requires undescribable references, which are visual concepts that are difficult to describe in language. However, we observe that many existing visual reasoning benchmarks are solvable with only describable text references. To close this gap, we introduce BrickVision, a new benchmark that requires undescribable visual references to solve.

articles.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
articles.content: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a different angle. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct agent ideas by directly measuring the distances between the agents' hidden state vectors. Crossover of ideas happens naturally in latent space, as a summarizer agent receives the combined KV caches of all swarm members. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve gets the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach the best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes. On several problems, SwarmEvolve with Qwen3 8B improves on the solutions that AlphaEvolve first found with frontier LLMs. Our work shows that agent swarms that communicate in latent space offer a fast, low-cost approach to program search for scientific problems.
